title: viable/strict/1794563420: [Inductor] optimized FakeTensor metadata refresh (#204337) (#204337)
excerpt: Summary: Human Summary The incremental update that's widely used in the Inductor post-grad passes currently scans all graph nodes with a node-hashing mechanism (based on the args, kwargs) to find changes. Although this is exhaustive and accurate, it is wasteful for compilation time if the caller already knows the root nodes where changes originated. Both updaters stop scheduling users when refreshed output metadata and storage semantics are unchanged; the targeted updater additionally compares aliasing against old and new arguments. The core implementation adds a sibling pass to the incremental_update function, which takes in the extra argument of which root nodes the change started from. It then performs the same propagation mechanisms as the original refresh helper. It also maintains the relevant FakeTensorUpdater states so that calls between this pass and the original are composable. The targeted updater processes a priority worklist in existing FX topological order. Starting from caller-supplied roots avoids the original graph-wide discovery scan, while early stopping bounds downstream propagation once metadata stabilizes. For K localized rewrites on an N-node graph, this replaces O(KN) full scans with work proportional to the affected regions; when those regions stay small, refresh cost is effectively O(K).
